<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# ⚠️ Warning: Availability Gate Failed

**The availability gate failed.** Measured availability was **99.1%**, below the **99.5%** threshold by **0.4 percentage points**.

The incident-duration gate passed. The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the 60-minute limit.

# Weekly Availability Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ **Fail** (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Pass (19 min margin) |
| Number of incidents | 2 | n/a | n/a |
| Total incident duration | 53 min (12 + 41) | n/a | n/a |

**Overall: Not met.** One of two gates failed.

### Note on the figures
The two incidents total 53 minutes. Over a 7-day week (10,080 minutes), that would mean about **99.47% availability**. The measured 99.1% implies about **91 minutes** of downtime, which leaves roughly **38 minutes unaccounted for** by the listed incidents. This may come from short or untracked disruptions, degraded-service periods counted against availability, or a different measurement window. It's worth checking, because even the 53 minutes of logged incidents alone would have missed the 99.5% gate. That target allows only about 50 minutes of downtime per week.
